resources.string: A tube of epithelium extends into the dermis and surrounds the root of the hair.
The duct of this eccrine gland carries sweat from its coiled base to a pore on the surface.
Blood vessels run through the dermis, not through the epidermis above it.
Flattened cells surrounded by lipids make up the outer barrier that limits water loss.
A pale layer beneath the stratum corneum is visible in the thick skin of palms and soles.
Flattening keratinocytes contain visible granules as they mature toward the surface.
Cell junctions hold neighboring keratinocytes together. They contribute to the spiny appearance seen under a microscope.
Dividing cells at the base supply new keratinocytes to the layers above.
Superficial loose connective tissue forms small projections into the base of the epidermis.
Small vascular loops reach into dermal papillae. Nutrients diffuse from the dermis into the overlying epidermis.
Thicker bundles of collagen and elastic fibers give the deeper dermis strength and flexibility.
Branches of sensory nerves pass through the dermis and carry signals from skin receptors.
